## 9. Glossary

- **OICP** — Open Inference Capabilities Protocol (v0.3). Wire
  types in `oicp-types`. A model publishes one `CapabilityClaim`
  per kind-of-work it does well; schedulers score requests against
  claims with shared protocol-level + per-scheduler operational
  adjustments. See [`docs/inference.md`](./docs/inference.md).
- **CapabilityHint** — Validated tag identifying a kind of work.
  Standardized: `general`, `code`. Open vocabulary via `x:<tag>`.
- **Recipe** — A TOML file in `sovereign-recipes` describing how
  to ingest one corpus end-to-end.
- **Registry** — The recipe catalog at
  `sovereign-recipes/registry.toml` (single source of truth).
  `corpus-engine`'s `build.rs` vendors it into `OUT_DIR` as the
  compile-time bundled snapshot; can refresh from GitHub at runtime.
- **DocumentFilter** — Trait between extract and chunk that drops
  `ExtractedDoc`s by predicate. Composable via `[[filter]]`.
- **FilterPipeline / ScopeMeta** — A recipe's filter set + its
  hash. Stored in `_corpus_meta.json`; lets a corpus expand in
  place by relaxing filters and delta-ingesting.
- **Field Model (v1)** — Five-phase enrichment (skeleton → cluster
  → align → fault lines → open questions) that analyses a corpus
  holistically rather than per-chunk.
- **Domain (v1)** — Trait encoding the epistemic conventions of a
  knowledge field (philosophy, personal, conversational, …). The single
  extension point for v1; only fully-implemented domains are registered.
- **Atlas (v2)** — Typed atom graph + `Pipeline` trait + registry +
  `ExemplarBank` + `PhaseCache`. See `ENRICHMENT_V2.md`. `PhaseCache`
  stamps each phase output with the producing model (`<phase>.model.json`
  sidecar) and declines to reuse a phase written by a different model —
  a model swap forces recomputation rather than silently mixing outputs
  (OICP v0.4 §6; keyed on `chat_model`, fingerprint deferred). Built via
  the single `EnrichConfig::phase_cache()` helper so all pipeline reads
  and writes carry the same identity.
- **SCIP** — Source Code Intelligence Protocol. `scip_graph.rs`
  stores SCIP data in SQLite; `scip_export.rs` dispatches to
  language-specific analyzers.
- **CodeWatcher** — `notify`-crate filesystem watcher. Re-indexes
  modified files via `CorpusEngine::reindex_file` and marks them
  stale in the call graph (800 ms debounce).
- **Shard** — A `corpus-engine` index containing only a contiguous
  chunk-ID range. Structurally identical to a complete index.
- **Skill** — A TOML file configuring routing triggers, planner
  templates, prompt overrides, memory rules, and OICP requirements
  for a class of work.
- **Slot** — A model-loading position in `EmbeddedLlamaCpp`
  (Quick / Main / Code / Embed). See
  [`docs/inference.md`](./docs/inference.md).
- **Mesh** — A closed trust ring of Commonwealth nodes that share
  inference and knowledge. Joined via a `cwth-XXXX-XXXX-XXXX` key.
- **Peering** — A trust relationship between two distinct meshes
  that lets them exchange models or knowledge under a chosen
  `PeerTrustLevel`.
- **EmbedFn / InferenceFn** — Function types `corpus-engine`
  accepts from its caller for embedding text and (optionally)
  running an LLM during enrichment. Keeps the engine free of any
  specific runtime.
- **EmbedModelInfo** — `{ model_id, dimensions, pooling,
  normalization }`. Cross-peer interoperability contract.
- **KnowledgeView** — Three-map landscape-digest system (personal
  memories, 180-day conversation history, institutional notes)
  spliced into the system prompt before each turn. Strict
  local-scope privacy is structural, not policy.
- **ATOS** — Agent Task Orchestration System. Two-layer
  scaffolding (project charter + per-feature specs) injecting the
  relevant contract into every agent turn, detecting SHA-256
  drift, recording decisions/deviations/milestones under
  `.sovereign/`.
- **Charter** — ATOS specification document (`CHARTER.md` for the
  project, `spec.md` for a feature). Committing it is approval.
- **Drift** — ATOS term for "spec file changed since approval."
  Warns next turn; does not block. Either revert or
  `atos spec accept`.
- **Sovereign-coder pipeline** — Commonwealth middleware chain
  (`approval_gate → session_briefing → context_injector →
  tool_injector → artifact_surface`) that adapts a generic coder
  model into an ATOS-aware one.
- **Work atlas** — Cross-mesh peer awareness:
  `work_in_flight` / `declare_scope` / `release_scope` MCP tools.
  See [`docs/WORK_ATLAS.md`](./docs/WORK_ATLAS.md).

[package]
name = "sovereign-inference"
version.workspace = true
edition.workspace = true
license.workspace = true

[dependencies]
sovereign-core = { workspace = true }
# The pure-HTTP OICP client (RemoteApiProvider / SplitInferenceProvider) was
# extracted here; re-exported at `sovereign_inference::remote::*`.
oicp-client = { workspace = true }
async-trait = { workspace = true }
serde = { workspace = true }
serde_json = { workspace = true }
thiserror = { workspace = true }
futures = { workspace = true }
tokio = { workspace = true }
tokio-util = { workspace = true }
sysinfo = "0.34"
# Cross-platform home-dir resolution (USERPROFILE on Windows, HOME on unix) for
# the RPC tensor-cache path. Matches sovereign-core's `dirs::home_dir()` usage.
dirs = "5"
encoding_rs = "0.8"
tracing = { workspace = true }
tokio-stream = "0.1"
reqwest = { workspace = true, features = ["stream"] }
# Parallel logit-mask in `json_constraint::mask`. Any model with a
# large vocab (Gemma-3-E4B ≈ 262K, Qwen3 ≈ 152K, Llama-3 ≈ 128K)
# pays a per-candidate validator cost on every generated token;
# running it serially on one core was the dominant Phase-1 latency.
rayon = "1.10"
# Jinja2 chat-template renderer. The llama-cpp-4 0.2.x binding
# dropped `apply_chat_template_oaicompat` (the bundled minja path),
# so models whose `tokenizer.chat_template` uses macros/sets
# (Gemma 3/4, Qwen3.5-9B-vOP) used to fall through to plain-text
# concat with hallucinated role markers + drifting stop tokens.
# See `embedded::apply_chat_template_minijinja`.
minijinja = { workspace = true }

# Re-adopted 2026-05-21 after the agent-bench sweep showed both
# observed failure classes (parse_failed_envelope, loop_trap) trace
# to the parser-leniency surface around free-form tool emission.
# llguidance's top-level alternation (`tool_envelope | plain_text`)
# closes both classes structurally. Used directly from Rust — the
# llama-cpp-4 binding's `LlamaSampler::llguidance` shim doesn't
# exist in 0.2.x, so we call llguidance from `ConstrainedSampler`
# alongside the existing in-house `JsonConstraint` mask.
llguidance = { workspace = true }

# llama.cpp's GPU backend is picked per-OS. Linux uses Vulkan because
# ROCm crashes in `ggml_cpu_extra_work_size` during Qwen3-A3B MoE
# inference on gfx1151 — a secondary CPU SEGV after a primary GPU
# memory fault. Upstream regression tracked at
# https://github.com/ggml-org/llama.cpp/issues/20176 (introduced by
# PR #20087); maintainer-acknowledged workaround in #19880 is to use
# the Vulkan backend, which is GPU-accelerated on the same hardware
# and bypasses the buggy ROCm+MoE path entirely. Revisit once #20176
# lands a fix in a llama-cpp-2 release we can pin to.
[target.'cfg(target_os = "macos")'.dependencies]
# llama-cpp-4 0.3.1 bundles llama.cpp 94a220cd6 (bumped from 0.2.57 / b9180
# on 2026-06-18). Includes MTP (Multi-Token Prediction, upstream PR #22673 —
# our original reason for moving off llama-cpp-2 0.1.146) plus the GLM-5
# long-context dense-mask overflow fix (#23610), the first build that runs
# glm_moe_dsa stably past ~200k tokens. See `crate::llama` for the migration
# shim that absorbs the API shape changes.
#
# default-features = false drops the vendored default `openmp` on macOS.
# Apple clang ships no OpenMP runtime, so the `openmp` feature makes
# llama-cpp-sys-4 hunt for a Homebrew libomp and build ggml with
# -DGGML_OPENMP=ON — which then links libomp.dylib, a NON-self-contained
# runtime dep the .app would have to bundle (the same -dylib trap the
# static-link cutover closed; see [[project_desktop_linux_build_deps]]).
# ggml's native pthread threadpool covers CPU ops without it, and Metal
# does the real work. We re-add `mtmd` (the other half of the vendored
# default). Linux keeps openmp below — libgomp is a standard system lib
# there, so it's a packageable dep, not a bundling problem.
llama-cpp-4 = { version = "0.4.2", default-features = false, features = ["metal", "mtmd"] }
# RPC distributed inference: enable the sys crate's `rpc` feature directly
# (builds ggml with GGML_RPC=ON + binds ggml_backend_rpc_add_server) rather
# than llama-cpp-4's `rpc` feature, whose binding module targets an older
# llama.cpp API (ggml_backend_rpc_add_device / 1-arg init) that no longer
# exists in the pinned llama.cpp. We call the sys symbols directly from
# embedded/model_slot.rs instead.
llama-cpp-sys-4 = { version = "0.4.2", features = ["rpc"] }

[target.'cfg(target_os = "linux")'.dependencies]
llama-cpp-4 = { version = "0.3.1", features = ["vulkan"] }
llama-cpp-sys-4 = { version = "0.3.1", features = ["rpc"] }

# Windows is the first OS that wants more than one backend, so unlike macOS
# (metal) / Linux (vulkan) — which hardcode their single backend above — the
# Windows backend is a CPU BASELINE plus feature-selected GPU layers (see the
# `[features]` block). CPU is the portable, SDK-free default that builds on the
# stock windows-2022 runner (preinstalled MSVC + CMake). Mirrors macOS's
# default-features=false + mtmd (CPU via ggml's pthread pool, no openmp dylib
# hunt); keeps the sys `rpc` feature so embedded/model_slot.rs's direct
# ggml_backend_rpc_add_server FFI links here too.
[target.'cfg(target_os = "windows")'.dependencies]
llama-cpp-4 = { version = "0.3.1", default-features = false, features = ["mtmd"] }
llama-cpp-sys-4 = { version = "0.3.1", features = ["rpc"] }

# Windows GPU backends layer onto the CPU baseline; the release matrix builds
# one variant per leg via `--features`. No-ops on macOS/Linux (which never pass
# them). `vulkan-1.dll` ships with the user's GPU driver, so the GPU loader is
# not bundled — only the BUILD needs the matching SDK (Vulkan SDK / CUDA Toolkit).
#   (default)                 -> CPU, universal
#   --features windows-vulkan -> NVIDIA + AMD + Intel GPU
#   --features windows-cuda   -> NVIDIA-optimized (deferred until benchmarks justify)
[features]
windows-vulkan = ["llama-cpp-4/vulkan"]
windows-cuda = ["llama-cpp-4/cuda"]

<!--
  SetupFlow — the only multi-step screen in the entire app.

  Listens to a single `setup-progress` Tauri event channel and invokes
  `complete_setup_auto`, which runs the whole setup chain (hardware probe
  → 3-model download → DB open → model load → smoke test) with no user
  choices. The actual rendering lives in `SetupScreen.svelte` (a pure,
  backend-free view) — this file is just the wiring that feeds it live
  progress. The dev screen gallery drives the same SetupScreen with
  per-phase fixtures, so you can audit every phase's copy without setup.

  No cancel button: closing the window pauses (downloads resume from
  `.part` on relaunch).
-->
<script lang="ts">
  import { onMount, onDestroy } from "svelte";
  import { listen, type UnlistenFn } from "@tauri-apps/api/event";
  import {
    completeSetupAuto,
    primaryCatalog,
    slotRecommendation,
    getConfig,
  } from "../api";
  import SetupScreen from "./SetupScreen.svelte";
  import type { Progress, Provenance, SlotProvenance } from "./setupTypes";

  interface Props {
    onComplete: () => void;
    /// The user's "Customize" primary-model choice from the Setup Plan
    /// screen (a catalog GGUF filename). Undefined = hardware-recommended.
    primaryFile?: string;
  }

  let { onComplete, primaryFile, primarySource }: Props = $props();

  const initialProgress: Progress = {
    phase: { kind: "detecting_hardware" },
    message: "Reading what this machine can do.",
    fraction: null,
    eta_seconds: null,
    indeterminate: true,
  };

  let progress = $state<Progress>({ ...initialProgress });
  let failed = $state<{ message: string; recoverable: boolean } | null>(null);
  let unlisten: UnlistenFn | null = null;

  // Read-only provenance for the ledger — what WILL download, from where, to
  // where. The setup-progress event carries only a generic message, so we
  // fetch this and SetupScreen joins it to the current phase. Best-effort:
  // if it fails the screen falls back to the plain phase messages.
  let provenance = $state<Provenance | null>(null);

  function slim(s: {
    base_name: string;
    file: string;
    quant: string;
    size_gb: number;
    hf_url: string;
  }): SlotProvenance {
    return {
      name: s.base_name || s.file,
      quant: s.quant,
      size_gb: s.size_gb,
      repo:
        (s.hf_url || "")
          .replace(/^https?:\/\/huggingface\.co\//, "")
          .replace(/\/$/, "") || "HuggingFace",
    };
  }

  async function loadProvenance() {
    try {
      const [cat, f, e, cfg] = await Promise.all([
        primaryCatalog(),
        slotRecommendation("fast"),
        slotRecommendation("embed"),
        getConfig().catch(() => null),
      ]);
      const prim =
        (primaryFile ? cat.find((o) => o.file === primaryFile) : null) ??
        cat.find((o) => o.recommended) ??
        cat[0] ??
        null;
      provenance = {
        modelsDir: cfg?.data_dir ? `${cfg.data_dir}/models` : "~/.svrnmesh/models",
        primary: prim ? slim(prim) : null,
        fast: f ? slim(f) : null,
        embed: e ? slim(e) : null,
      };
    } catch {
      // Ledger degrades to the generic phase messages — non-fatal.
    }
  }

  onMount(async () => {
    unlisten = await listen<Progress>("setup-progress", (e) => {
      progress = e.payload;
      if (e.payload.phase.kind === "failed") {
        failed = {
          message: e.payload.message,
          recoverable: e.payload.phase.recoverable,
        };
      } else {
        failed = null;
      }
    });
    void loadProvenance();
    try {
      await completeSetupAuto(primaryFile, primarySource);
      onComplete();
    } catch (e) {
      // Backend will already have emitted Failed; this catch handles
      // the pathological case where it didn't.
      if (!failed) {
        failed = { message: String(e), recoverable: false };
      }
    }
  });

  onDestroy(() => {
    unlisten?.();
  });

  async function retry() {
    failed = null;
    progress = { ...initialProgress };
    try {
      await completeSetupAuto(primaryFile);
      onComplete();
    } catch (e) {
      if (!failed) {
        failed = { message: String(e), recoverable: false };
      }
    }
  }
</script>

<SetupScreen {progress} {failed} {provenance} onRetry={retry} />

# models.toml — Sovereign Model Manifest
#
# Source of truth for slot configuration per hardware profile.
# The hardware detector selects a profile; the setup/download flow reads
# this file to know which files to fetch and which family to assign.
#
# Each slot entry specifies:
#   repo        HuggingFace repo ID (for download)
#   file        Exact GGUF filename within that repo
#   family      ModelFamily variant (drives default quirks)
#   quant       Quantisation label (informational, for display)
#   size_gb     Approximate on-disk size after download
#   thinking    Whether this slot uses thinking mode (bool)
#               Fast slot: always false
#               Thoughtful slot: true unless family is AlwaysOn or None
#   hf_url      Direct link for the developer/user
#
# Optional [profiles.X.Y.quirks_override] tables override individual
# fields from the family's default_quirks(). Only specify what differs.
#
# Optional [profiles.X.Y.capabilities] tables declare the slot's OICP
# capability profile (per spec §2.4, levels 0..=4 = none/basic/moderate/
# strong/exceptional). Consumed by `sovereign-mesh` to score backends
# when routing synthesis across a Commonwealth mesh — a Joiner running
# a 1.7B picks the Founder's 30B-A3B for `Analysis ≥ 3` requests, etc.
# Absent = BYOM / legacy: mesh routing falls back to conservative
# defaults. Capabilities: general, code, analysis, math, creative,
# instruction, multilingual, vision, long_context (snake_case keys).
#
# Optional `base_name` field identifies the model across quantisation
# and repo variants. A slot declaring `base_name = "Qwen3-30B-A3B"` will
# be used for ANY GGUF whose filename contains that string — so the
# same capability row covers Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, Q8_0, unsloth's
# `Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf`, and a local re-quant.
# Longest base_name match wins when multiple would apply.
#
# ── Curation philosophy (2026-05) ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Cross-platform speed reference informed this revision: Strix Halo 128GB
# (unified memory), Mac M2 Max 64GB (unified memory), and an RTX 4060 8GB
# (discrete, hard 8GB VRAM wall). The discrete-GPU case is what shapes
# the `default` profile's choice — MoE models like 30B-A3B spill across
# the PCIe bus on 8GB GPUs and lose their speed advantage, so dense 8B
# is the right thoughtful pick for that tier.
#
# We standardise on `unsloth/*-GGUF` for chat/instruct GGUFs (preferred
# over bartowski for fresh re-quants; fixes for tokenizer issues land
# there first). Embeddings stay on the official `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-*`
# repos — no quality reason to re-host.
#
# ── Fast slot notes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Fast does intent classification + JSON routing, not synthesis. We don't
# scale it up with hardware — a larger router buys nothing for routing
# quality and wastes always-resident VRAM. Stays on Qwen3 0.6B/1.7B
# across all profiles. Qwen3-1.7B is the well-validated choice for
# structured JSON output at this size.
#
# ── Thoughtful slot notes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `default` (8–19 GB VRAM): Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M (~5 GB). The universal
# daily driver — fits fully in any 8GB+ GPU's VRAM, ~42 t/s on RTX 4060,
# strong JSON grammar compliance under llama.cpp. /no_think mode
# (`thinking = false`) eliminates wasted reasoning tokens for the
# structured tasks that dominate routing-mediated chat.
#
# `high`/`very_high` (≥20 GB VRAM, unified memory tier): Qwen3-30B-A3B
# Thinking-2507. The MoE sweet spot for unified-memory systems — 3B
# active params at ~86 t/s on Strix Halo, ~100 t/s on M2 Max. We
# only select this profile when ≥20 GB free is detected, otherwise
# fall through to default to avoid the PCIe-spill failure mode that
# kills MoE perf on 8GB discrete GPUs.
#
# ── Embed slot notes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Qwen3-Embedding is purpose-built for retrieval. The 0.6B model is used
# always-resident for cpu_only/low_mem/default; 4B for high/very_high.
# Stays on the official `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-*` repos.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# models.toml — Sovereign Model Manifest
#
# Source of truth for slot configuration per hardware profile.
# The hardware detector selects a profile; the setup/download flow reads
# this file to know which files to fetch and which family to assign.
#
# Each slot entry specifies:
#   repo        HuggingFace repo ID (for download)
#   file        Exact GGUF filename within that repo
#   family      ModelFamily variant (drives default quirks)
#   quant       Quantisation label (informational, for display)
#   size_gb     Approximate on-disk size after download
#   thinking    Whether this slot uses thinking mode (bool)
#               Fast slot: always false
#               Thoughtful slot: true unless family is AlwaysOn or None
#   hf_url      Direct link for the developer/user
#
# Optional [profiles.X.Y.quirks_override] tables override individual
# fields from the family's default_quirks(). Only specify what differs.
#
# Optional [profiles.X.Y.capabilities] tables declare the slot's OICP
# capability profile (per spec §2.4, levels 0..=4 = none/basic/moderate/
# strong/exceptional). Consumed by `sovereign-mesh` to score backends
# when routing synthesis across a Commonwealth mesh — a Joiner running
# a 1.7B picks the Founder's 30B-A3B for `Analysis ≥ 3` requests, etc.
# Absent = BYOM / legacy: mesh routing falls back to conservative
# defaults. Capabilities: general, code, analysis, math, creative,
# instruction, multilingual, vision, long_context (snake_case keys).
#
# Optional `base_name` field identifies the model across quantisation
# and repo variants. A slot declaring `base_name = "Qwen3-30B-A3B"` will
# be used for ANY GGUF whose filename contains that string — so the
# same capability row covers Q4_K_M, Q5_K_M, Q8_0, unsloth's
# `Qwen3-30B-A3B-Thinking-2507-Q4_K_M.gguf`, and a local re-quant.
# Longest base_name match wins when multiple would apply.
#
# ── Curation philosophy (2026-05) ────────────────────────────────────────────
# Cross-platform speed reference informed this revision: Strix Halo 128GB
# (unified memory), Mac M2 Max 64GB (unified memory), and an RTX 4060 8GB
# (discrete, hard 8GB VRAM wall). The discrete-GPU case is what shapes
# the `default` profile's choice — MoE models like 30B-A3B spill across
# the PCIe bus on 8GB GPUs and lose their speed advantage, so dense 8B
# is the right thoughtful pick for that tier.
#
# We standardise on `unsloth/*-GGUF` for chat/instruct GGUFs (preferred
# over bartowski for fresh re-quants; fixes for tokenizer issues land
# there first). Embeddings stay on the official `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-*`
# repos — no quality reason to re-host.
#
# ── Fast slot notes ──────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Fast does intent classification + JSON routing, not synthesis. We don't
# scale it up with hardware — a larger router buys nothing for routing
# quality and wastes always-resident VRAM. Stays on Qwen3 0.6B/1.7B
# across all profiles. Qwen3-1.7B is the well-validated choice for
# structured JSON output at this size.
#
# ── Thoughtful slot notes ────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# `default` (8–19 GB VRAM): Qwen3-8B Q4_K_M (~5 GB). The universal
# daily driver — fits fully in any 8GB+ GPU's VRAM, ~42 t/s on RTX 4060,
# strong JSON grammar compliance under llama.cpp. /no_think mode
# (`thinking = false`) eliminates wasted reasoning tokens for the
# structured tasks that dominate routing-mediated chat.
#
# `high`/`very_high` (≥20 GB VRAM, unified memory tier): Qwen3-30B-A3B
# Thinking-2507. The MoE sweet spot for unified-memory systems — 3B
# active params at ~86 t/s on Strix Halo, ~100 t/s on M2 Max. We
# only select this profile when ≥20 GB free is detected, otherwise
# fall through to default to avoid the PCIe-spill failure mode that
# kills MoE perf on 8GB discrete GPUs.
#
# ── Embed slot notes ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────
# Qwen3-Embedding is purpose-built for retrieval. The 0.6B model is used
# always-resident for cpu_only/low_mem/default; 4B for high/very_high.
# Stays on the official `Qwen/Qwen3-Embedding-*` repos.
# ─────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────────

# Workspace CI — the unified root workspace (40 crates: oicp-types,
# corpus-engine + carve-outs + xtask, sovereign/*, commonwealth/*).
#
# Why this lives at the repo root: GitHub Actions only executes workflows in
# the *root* `.github/workflows/`. `commonwealth/.github/workflows/ci.yml` is a
# leftover from when commonwealth was its own repo and NEVER runs — this file
# replaces it. Before this landed the only active workflow was desktop-release,
# i.e. there was no continuous check/test gate at all.
#
# Gate policy (contributor-facing — a commit to main only goes red for
# genuine quality regressions):

#     their burn-in month (quality program, 2026-07); each flips blocking by
#     deleting its continue-on-error line after ~4 clean weeks.

#                anywhere is a 0→1 count growth and fails the gate, while
#                the grandfathered stock burns down via --tighten. The
#                2026-07-12 sweep (`cargo clippy --fix` + agents) cleared
#                the mechanical debt.

name: CI

on:
  push:
    branches: [main]
  pull_request:
    branches: [main]
  # No-op until a merge queue is enabled in repo settings; landing the
  # trigger now makes enabling one a settings flip, not a workflow PR.
  merge_group:

# Cancel superseded runs of the same PR (a force-push mid-run otherwise
# burns a full workspace build). Never cancel main's post-merge runs —
# they are the sole writers of the shared caches.
concurrency:
  group: ci-${{ github.ref }}
  cancel-in-progress: ${{ github.event_name == 'pull_request' }}

env:
  CARGO_TERM_COLOR: always
  # No debuginfo in CI builds: debuginfo is the bulk of a debug target/'s
  # bytes, and the hosted runner died with "No space left on device" mid
  # llama.cpp build (2026-07-02). Symbol names survive (backtraces stay
  # readable, just without line numbers); reproduce locally for real
  # debugging. Also keeps the shared rust-cache within GitHub's 10 GB
  # per-repo cache budget.
  CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG: "0"
  CARGO_PROFILE_TEST_DEBUG: "0"

jobs:
  # ONE workspace compile per run. `check --all-targets` and `test` share a
  # target/ tree in the same job (check adds only rmeta for benches on top of
  # the test build); the old separate check job paid the whole llama.cpp +
  # workspace build a second time. This job is also the ONLY writer of the
  # shared `workspace` cache — mesh-dst and clippy restore it read-only, so
  # the heavy dependency artifacts (llama-cpp-sys' cmake/ggml output above
  # all) compile at most once per lockfile change across the whole matrix.

    name: Check + Test (workspace)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # The workspace build + restored cache + apt stack don't fit in the
      # runner's ~20 GB of free disk (observed: compiler scratch in /tmp hit
      # ENOSPC mid llama.cpp build). Drop ~30 GB of preinstalled images we
      # never use before compiling anything.
      - name: Free runner disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /usr/local/.ghcup /opt/hostedtoolcache \
            /usr/share/swift /usr/local/share/boost 2>/dev/null || true
          sudo docker image prune --all --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          # The hosted runner has a second, mostly-empty ~65 GB scratch disk
          # at /mnt. Bind-mount target/ onto it (caches still work — tar sees
          # a plain dir) and point TMPDIR there too, so neither the build tree
          # nor compiler scratch can fill the root disk again.
          sudo mkdir -p /mnt/target /mnt/tmp
          sudo chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /mnt/target /mnt/tmp
          mkdir -p target
          sudo mount --bind /mnt/target target
          echo "TMPDIR=/mnt/tmp" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          df -h / /mnt | tail -2
      # rust-toolchain.toml pins the exact version; the bare install
      # command reads it (no version strings in workflow YAML).
      - name: Install pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml)
        run: rustup toolchain install
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          shared-key: workspace
          # Seed the cache even on a red run — otherwise a failing test
          # keeps every subsequent run cold (rust-cache skips its save
          # step on failure by default; that is exactly how this CI
          # stayed cold for weeks).
          cache-on-failure: true
      # rust-cache's save-time cleanup prunes unrecognized dirs under
      # target/ — which would delete target/llama-cmake-cache (the shared
      # CMake tree llama-cpp-sys links against) while KEEPING the crate's
      # "already built" fingerprint: a poisoned cache that link-fails on
      # every warm run. Cache the tree separately. Restore/save are split
      # so the save (an explicit step below, `if: always()`) seeds the
      # cache even when check/test fail — while CI is stabilizing, a red
      # run must still bank the 20-minute C++ build. The C++ is
      # CMAKE_BUILD_TYPE=Release regardless of cargo profile, so this key
      # also serves the release workflows.

        id: llama-cache
        uses: actions/cache/restore@v6
        with:
          path: target/llama-cmake-cache
          key: llama-cmake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
      # Belt: if the tree is missing while the fingerprint survived
      # (partial restore / LRU eviction), force the build script to rerun
      # rather than link against nothing.
      - name: Guard llama fingerprint vs missing CMake tree
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if ! ls target/llama-cmake-cache/*/lib*/libllama.* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            rm -rf target/*/.fingerprint/llama-cpp-sys-4-* 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
      # The workspace needs the full Linux native stack (mirrors
      # desktop-release.yml — keep in sync):
      #   mold + clang        — pinned as the Linux linker by .cargo/config.toml;
      #                         without ld.mold every link dies with
      #                         "invalid linker name in argument '-fuse-ld=mold'".
      #   protoc + libprotobuf — lance-encoding's prost-build.
      #   Vulkan SDK (LunarG) — sovereign-inference hardcodes llama-cpp-4's
      #                         `vulkan` feature on Linux, so ggml builds with
      #                         GGML_VULKAN=ON and needs glslc (shaderc),
      #                         spirv-headers, libvulkan even for `cargo check`.
      #   webkit2gtk et al.   — sovereign-desktop/src-tauri is a workspace member.
      - name: System deps
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl gnupg
          curl -fsSL https://packages.lunarg.com/lunarg-signing-key-pub.asc \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/lunarg.asc >/dev/null
          curl -fsSL "https://packages.lunarg.com/vulkan/lunarg-vulkan-$(lsb_release -cs).list" \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/lunarg-vulkan.list >/dev/null
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            protobuf-compiler libprotobuf-dev cmake mold clang \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libappindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev \
            libvulkan-dev vulkan-headers spirv-headers spirv-tools shaderc
      # check first: fails fast on type errors (rmeta only, covers benches
      # via --all-targets); test then reuses the same dependency artifacts.
      - run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets
      # Tests are CI-safe by contract (no GPU / network / model weights —
      # ARCH_PRINCIPLES §12.4): DeterministicInference + in-memory SQLite + FTS5.
      # (The Vulkan SDK above is a BUILD dep of ggml; tests still run CPU-only.)
      # -j 3: the tail of this build links dozens of integration-test binaries,
      # each statically linking the llama+ggml-vulkan archives — four parallel
      # mold links can OOM the 16 GB runner hard enough to kill the runner
      # agent itself (the "log just stops, no artifacts" failure, 2026-07-02).
      - run: cargo test --workspace -j 3
      # Bank the C++ build even on a red run (see the restore step's comment).
      - name: Save llama.cpp CMake tree
        if: always() && steps.llama-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v6
        with:
          path: target/llama-cmake-cache
          key: llama-cmake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
      # When something dies, say WHICH resource died — the ENOSPC failure
      # (2026-07-02) surfaced as a bare "error writing /tmp/…: No space left"
      # deep in a C++ trace.

        run: |

          # nor compiler scratch can fill the root disk again.

      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2

          # (incl. the llama.cpp cmake output) is reused. save-if false so

        uses: actions/cache@v6
        with:

      - name: Guard llama fingerprint vs missing CMake tree
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if ! ls target/llama-cmake-cache/*/lib*/libllama.* >/dev/null 2>&1; then

          fi
      # sovereign-mesh pulls sovereign-inference → the Vulkan build stack is
      # needed here too (no gtk: the desktop crate isn't in this dep tree).

        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl gnupg
          curl -fsSL https://packages.lunarg.com/lunarg-signing-key-pub.asc \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/lunarg.asc >/dev/null

            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/lunarg-vulkan.list >/dev/null

          sudo apt-get install -y \
            protobuf-compiler libprotobuf-dev cmake mold clang \
            libvulkan-dev vulkan-headers spirv-headers spirv-tools shaderc
      # Deterministic-simulation mesh suite (Layer 1 of commonwealth/docs/MESH_QA.md):
      # drives REAL gossip under a per-node FaultTransport + seeded fault schedule
      # and asserts the invariant pack. In-process — no GPU/network/weights, CI-safe.
      # `treesitter` alongside `dst` is FEATURE-UNIFICATION HYGIENE, not a test
      # need: the restored `workspace` cache was built with corpus-engine's
      # treesitter feature on (the daemon/server/cli members require it); a bare
      # `-p sovereign-mesh` build resolves it OFF, so cargo rebuilt corpus-engine
      # + its 17 dependents from scratch on every run. Matching the feature set
      # makes the cache actually hit.
      - run: cargo test -p sovereign-mesh --features dst,treesitter --test dst_scenarios

  # One runner for every xtask gate (each runs in <1s once xtask compiles;
  # they used to be two jobs paying the setup twice). Blocking/advisory is
  # per-STEP: boundary-gate keeps its blocking status; the gates landed by
  # the quality program (2026-07-11: layer, lock, re-baselined arch) run
  # advisory for a burn-in month — flip each by deleting its
  # `continue-on-error` line. Local equivalent: `cargo xtask quality`.
  gates:
    name: Gates (boundary / arch / layer / lock)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # rust-toolchain.toml pins the exact version; the bare install
      # command reads it (no version strings in workflow YAML).
      - name: Install pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml)
        run: rustup toolchain install
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          # xtask + arch-layers + their handful of deps only — shared with
          # docs-reconcile's docs-gate job, which builds the identical tree.
          shared-key: xtask
      # No protoc/cmake needed — xtask only reads files. mold + clang ARE
      # needed: compiling xtask itself links through the pinned ld.mold.
      - name: System deps
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y mold clang
      # NOT advisory: a boundary breach means the workflow/recipe package can
      # no longer be lifted out against just the OICP contract
      # (studio/BOUNDARY.md).
      - name: boundary-gate (blocking)
        run: cargo run -p xtask -- boundary-gate
      - name: arch-gate (advisory — burn-in until ~2026-08)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo run -p xtask -- arch-gate
      - name: layer-gate (advisory — burn-in until ~2026-08)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo run -p xtask -- layer-gate
      - name: lock-gate (advisory — burn-in until ~2026-08)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo run -p xtask -- lock-gate

  # Supply-chain policy (deny.toml). Metadata-only — no compile, ~1 min.
  # Advisory for its burn-in month (quality program, 2026-07-11), then the
  # licenses/bans/sources step flips blocking. The advisories lane stays
  # permanently non-blocking on PRs: it reads the moving RustSec DB, so a
  # brand-new CVE would otherwise red-X unrelated contributor PRs — the
  # weekly lane owns paging the owner about those.
  deny:
    name: Deny (licenses / bans / sources, advisory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Licenses, bans, sources (deterministic vs Cargo.lock)
        uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2
        with:
          command: check licenses bans sources
      - name: Advisories (informational — never blocks)
        uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          command: check advisories

  fmt:
    name: Format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # rust-toolchain.toml pins the exact version + carries the rustfmt
      # component; the bare install command reads it.
      - name: Install pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml)
        run: rustup toolchain install
      # BLOCKING since the 2026-07-02 `cargo fmt --all` sweep (404 files,
      # listed in .git-blame-ignore-revs) zeroed the format debt. Runs in
      # seconds (no compilation); a failure diff is now one contributor's
      # change, small and actionable.
      - run: cargo fmt --all --check

  clippy:
    name: Clippy (advisory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # Same disk headroom problem as the test job — see its comment.
      - name: Free runner disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /usr/local/.ghcup /opt/hostedtoolcache \
            /usr/share/swift /usr/local/share/boost 2>/dev/null || true
          sudo docker image prune --all --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          # The hosted runner has a second, mostly-empty ~65 GB scratch disk
          # at /mnt. Bind-mount target/ onto it (caches still work — tar sees
          # a plain dir) and point TMPDIR there too, so neither the build tree
          # nor compiler scratch can fill the root disk again.
          sudo mkdir -p /mnt/target /mnt/tmp
          sudo chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /mnt/target /mnt/tmp
          mkdir -p target
          sudo mount --bind /mnt/target target
          echo "TMPDIR=/mnt/tmp" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          df -h / /mnt | tail -2
      # rust-toolchain.toml pins the exact version + carries the clippy
      # component; the bare install command reads it.
      - name: Install pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml)
        run: rustup toolchain install
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          # Reuse the test job's dependency artifacts (clippy re-lints the
          # workspace crates with clippy-driver, but deps compile normally
          # and hit the cache). Read-only: advisory lanes never write.
          shared-key: workspace
          save-if: false
      # See the test job: the CMake tree is cached separately from
      # rust-cache (whose cleanup would delete it), and the guard forces a
      # rebuild instead of a link failure if the tree is missing.
      - name: Cache llama.cpp CMake tree
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: target/llama-cmake-cache
          key: llama-cmake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
      - name: Guard llama fingerprint vs missing CMake tree
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if ! ls target/llama-cmake-cache/*/lib*/libllama.* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            rm -rf target/*/.fingerprint/llama-cpp-sys-4-* 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
      # Same native stack as the check+test job (see its comment) — keep in sync.
      - name: System deps
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl gnupg
          curl -fsSL https://packages.lunarg.com/lunarg-signing-key-pub.asc \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/lunarg.asc >/dev/null

            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/lunarg-vulkan.list >/dev/null

          sudo apt-get install -y \
            protobuf-compiler libprotobuf-dev cmake mold clang \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libappindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev \
            libvulkan-dev vulkan-headers spirv-headers spirv-tools shaderc
      # JSON stream feeds the lint-gate count ratchet: per-(crate, lint)
      # warning counts may never grow vs quality/baselines/clippy_counts.tsv.

      - name: Clippy (JSON)
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --message-format=json > /tmp/clippy.json
      - name: lint-gate (count ratchet)
        run: cargo run -p xtask -- lint-gate --from /tmp/clippy.json

        with:
          path: target/llama-cmake-cache
          key: llama-cmake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
      # Belt: if the tree is missing while the fingerprint survived
      # (partial restore / LRU eviction), force the build script to rerun
      # rather than link against nothing.
      - name: Guard llama fingerprint vs missing CMake tree
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if ! ls target/llama-cmake-cache/*/lib*/libllama.* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            rm -rf target/*/.fingerprint/llama-cpp-sys-4-* 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
      # The workspace needs the full Linux native stack (mirrors
      # desktop-release.yml — keep in sync):
      #   mold + clang        — pinned as the Linux linker by .cargo/config.toml;
      #                         without ld.mold every link dies with
      #                         "invalid linker name in argument '-fuse-ld=mold'".
      #   protoc + libprotobuf — lance-encoding's prost-build.
      #   Vulkan SDK (LunarG) — sovereign-inference hardcodes llama-cpp-4's
      #                         `vulkan` feature on Linux, so ggml builds with
      #                         GGML_VULKAN=ON and needs glslc (shaderc),
      #                         spirv-headers, libvulkan even for `cargo check`.
      #   webkit2gtk et al.   — sovereign-desktop/src-tauri is a workspace member.
      - name: System deps
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl gnupg
          curl -fsSL https://packages.lunarg.com/lunarg-signing-key-pub.asc \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/lunarg.asc >/dev/null
          curl -fsSL "https://packages.lunarg.com/vulkan/lunarg-vulkan-$(lsb_release -cs).list" \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/lunarg-vulkan.list >/dev/null
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            protobuf-compiler libprotobuf-dev cmake mold clang \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libappindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev \
            libvulkan-dev vulkan-headers spirv-headers spirv-tools shaderc
      # check first: fails fast on type errors (rmeta only, covers benches
      # via --all-targets); test then reuses the same dependency artifacts.
      - run: cargo check --workspace --all-targets
      # Tests are CI-safe by contract (no GPU / network / model weights —
      # ARCH_PRINCIPLES §12.4): DeterministicInference + in-memory SQLite + FTS5.
      # (The Vulkan SDK above is a BUILD dep of ggml; tests still run CPU-only.)
      # -j 3: the tail of this build links dozens of integration-test binaries,
      # each statically linking the llama+ggml-vulkan archives — four parallel
      # mold links can OOM the 16 GB runner hard enough to kill the runner
      # agent itself (the "log just stops, no artifacts" failure, 2026-07-02).
      - run: cargo test --workspace -j 3
      # Bank the C++ build even on a red run (see the restore step's comment).
      - name: Save llama.cpp CMake tree
        if: always() && steps.llama-cache.outputs.cache-hit != 'true'
        uses: actions/cache/save@v4
        with:
          path: target/llama-cmake-cache
          key: llama-cmake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
      # When something dies, say WHICH resource died — the ENOSPC failure
      # (2026-07-02) surfaced as a bare "error writing /tmp/…: No space left"
      # deep in a C++ trace.
      - name: Resource state at failure
        if: failure()
        run: df -h; echo; free -h; echo; du -sh target 2>/dev/null || true

  mesh-dst:
    name: Mesh DST (fault-injection / invariants)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      # Same disk headroom problem as the test job — see its comment.
      - name: Free runner disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /usr/local/.ghcup /opt/hostedtoolcache \
            /usr/share/swift /usr/local/share/boost 2>/dev/null || true
          sudo docker image prune --all --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          # The hosted runner has a second, mostly-empty ~65 GB scratch disk
          # at /mnt. Bind-mount target/ onto it (caches still work — tar sees
          # a plain dir) and point TMPDIR there too, so neither the build tree
          # nor compiler scratch can fill the root disk again.
          sudo mkdir -p /mnt/target /mnt/tmp
          sudo chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /mnt/target /mnt/tmp
          mkdir -p target
          sudo mount --bind /mnt/target target
          echo "TMPDIR=/mnt/tmp" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          df -h / /mnt | tail -2
      # rust-toolchain.toml pins the exact version; the bare install
      # command reads it (no version strings in workflow YAML).
      - name: Install pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml)
        run: rustup toolchain install
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          # Restore the test job's cache read-only: the `dst` feature set
          # recompiles sovereign-mesh itself, but every dependency artifact
          # (incl. the llama.cpp cmake output) is reused. save-if false so
          # this feature-skewed tree never overwrites the canonical cache.
          shared-key: workspace
          save-if: false
      # See the test job: the CMake tree is cached separately from
      # rust-cache (whose cleanup would delete it), and the guard forces a
      # rebuild instead of a link failure if the tree is missing.
      - name: Cache llama.cpp CMake tree

          key: llama-cmake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}

        shell: bash
        run: |
          if ! ls target/llama-cmake-cache/*/lib*/libllama.* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            rm -rf target/*/.fingerprint/llama-cpp-sys-4-* 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
      # sovereign-mesh pulls sovereign-inference → the Vulkan build stack is
      # needed here too (no gtk: the desktop crate isn't in this dep tree).
      - name: System deps
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl gnupg
          curl -fsSL https://packages.lunarg.com/lunarg-signing-key-pub.asc \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/lunarg.asc >/dev/null
          curl -fsSL "https://packages.lunarg.com/vulkan/lunarg-vulkan-$(lsb_release -cs).list" \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/lunarg-vulkan.list >/dev/null
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            protobuf-compiler libprotobuf-dev cmake mold clang \
            libvulkan-dev vulkan-headers spirv-headers spirv-tools shaderc
      # Deterministic-simulation mesh suite (Layer 1 of commonwealth/docs/MESH_QA.md):
      # drives REAL gossip under a per-node FaultTransport + seeded fault schedule
      # and asserts the invariant pack. In-process — no GPU/network/weights, CI-safe.
      # `treesitter` alongside `dst` is FEATURE-UNIFICATION HYGIENE, not a test
      # need: the restored `workspace` cache was built with corpus-engine's
      # treesitter feature on (the daemon/server/cli members require it); a bare
      # `-p sovereign-mesh` build resolves it OFF, so cargo rebuilt corpus-engine
      # + its 17 dependents from scratch on every run. Matching the feature set
      # makes the cache actually hit.
      - run: cargo test -p sovereign-mesh --features dst,treesitter --test dst_scenarios

  # One runner for every xtask gate (each runs in <1s once xtask compiles;
  # they used to be two jobs paying the setup twice). Blocking/advisory is
  # per-STEP: boundary-gate keeps its blocking status; the gates landed by
  # the quality program (2026-07-11: layer, lock, re-baselined arch) run
  # advisory for a burn-in month — flip each by deleting its
  # `continue-on-error` line. Local equivalent: `cargo xtask quality`.
  gates:
    name: Gates (boundary / arch / layer / lock)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v7
      # rust-toolchain.toml pins the exact version; the bare install
      # command reads it (no version strings in workflow YAML).
      - name: Install pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml)
        run: rustup toolchain install
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          # xtask + arch-layers + their handful of deps only — shared with
          # docs-reconcile's docs-gate job, which builds the identical tree.
          shared-key: xtask
      # No protoc/cmake needed — xtask only reads files. mold + clang ARE
      # needed: compiling xtask itself links through the pinned ld.mold.
      - name: System deps
        run: sudo apt-get update && sudo apt-get install -y mold clang
      # NOT advisory: a boundary breach means the workflow/recipe package can
      # no longer be lifted out against just the OICP contract
      # (studio/BOUNDARY.md).
      - name: boundary-gate (blocking)
        run: cargo run -p xtask -- boundary-gate
      - name: arch-gate (advisory — burn-in until ~2026-08)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo run -p xtask -- arch-gate
      - name: layer-gate (advisory — burn-in until ~2026-08)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo run -p xtask -- layer-gate
      - name: lock-gate (advisory — burn-in until ~2026-08)
        continue-on-error: true
        run: cargo run -p xtask -- lock-gate

  # Supply-chain policy (deny.toml). Metadata-only — no compile, ~1 min.
  # Advisory for its burn-in month (quality program, 2026-07-11), then the
  # licenses/bans/sources step flips blocking. The advisories lane stays
  # permanently non-blocking on PRs: it reads the moving RustSec DB, so a
  # brand-new CVE would otherwise red-X unrelated contributor PRs — the
  # weekly lane owns paging the owner about those.
  deny:
    name: Deny (licenses / bans / sources, advisory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      - name: Licenses, bans, sources (deterministic vs Cargo.lock)
        uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2
        with:
          command: check licenses bans sources
      - name: Advisories (informational — never blocks)
        uses: EmbarkStudios/cargo-deny-action@v2
        continue-on-error: true
        with:
          command: check advisories

  fmt:
    name: Format
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # rust-toolchain.toml pins the exact version + carries the rustfmt
      # component; the bare install command reads it.
      - name: Install pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml)
        run: rustup toolchain install
      # BLOCKING since the 2026-07-02 `cargo fmt --all` sweep (404 files,
      # listed in .git-blame-ignore-revs) zeroed the format debt. Runs in
      # seconds (no compilation); a failure diff is now one contributor's
      # change, small and actionable.
      - run: cargo fmt --all --check

  clippy:
    name: Clippy (advisory)
    runs-on: ubuntu-latest
    continue-on-error: true
    steps:
      - uses: actions/checkout@v4
      # Same disk headroom problem as the test job — see its comment.
      - name: Free runner disk space
        run: |
          sudo rm -rf /usr/share/dotnet /usr/local/lib/android /opt/ghc \
            /usr/local/.ghcup /opt/hostedtoolcache \
            /usr/share/swift /usr/local/share/boost 2>/dev/null || true
          sudo docker image prune --all --force >/dev/null 2>&1 || true
          # The hosted runner has a second, mostly-empty ~65 GB scratch disk
          # at /mnt. Bind-mount target/ onto it (caches still work — tar sees
          # a plain dir) and point TMPDIR there too, so neither the build tree
          # nor compiler scratch can fill the root disk again.
          sudo mkdir -p /mnt/target /mnt/tmp
          sudo chown "$(id -u):$(id -g)" /mnt/target /mnt/tmp
          mkdir -p target
          sudo mount --bind /mnt/target target
          echo "TMPDIR=/mnt/tmp" >> "$GITHUB_ENV"
          df -h / /mnt | tail -2
      # rust-toolchain.toml pins the exact version + carries the clippy
      # component; the bare install command reads it.
      - name: Install pinned toolchain (rust-toolchain.toml)
        run: rustup toolchain install
      - uses: Swatinem/rust-cache@v2
        with:
          # Reuse the test job's dependency artifacts (clippy re-lints the
          # workspace crates with clippy-driver, but deps compile normally
          # and hit the cache). Read-only: advisory lanes never write.
          shared-key: workspace
          save-if: false
      # See the test job: the CMake tree is cached separately from
      # rust-cache (whose cleanup would delete it), and the guard forces a
      # rebuild instead of a link failure if the tree is missing.
      - name: Cache llama.cpp CMake tree
        uses: actions/cache@v4
        with:
          path: target/llama-cmake-cache
          key: llama-cmake-${{ runner.os }}-${{ runner.arch }}-${{ hashFiles('Cargo.lock') }}
      - name: Guard llama fingerprint vs missing CMake tree
        shell: bash
        run: |
          if ! ls target/llama-cmake-cache/*/lib*/libllama.* >/dev/null 2>&1; then
            rm -rf target/*/.fingerprint/llama-cpp-sys-4-* 2>/dev/null || true
          fi
      # Same native stack as the check+test job (see its comment) — keep in sync.
      - name: System deps
        run: |
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y ca-certificates curl gnupg
          curl -fsSL https://packages.lunarg.com/lunarg-signing-key-pub.asc \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/trusted.gpg.d/lunarg.asc >/dev/null
          curl -fsSL "https://packages.lunarg.com/vulkan/lunarg-vulkan-$(lsb_release -cs).list" \
            | sudo tee /etc/apt/sources.list.d/lunarg-vulkan.list >/dev/null
          sudo apt-get update
          sudo apt-get install -y \
            protobuf-compiler libprotobuf-dev cmake mold clang \
            libwebkit2gtk-4.1-dev libappindicator3-dev librsvg2-dev \
            libvulkan-dev vulkan-headers spirv-headers spirv-tools shaderc
      # JSON stream feeds the lint-gate count ratchet: per-(crate, lint)
      # warning counts may never grow vs quality/baselines/clippy_counts.tsv.
      # Old debt burns down crate by crate; new debt is blocked.
      - name: Clippy (JSON)
        run: cargo clippy --workspace --all-targets --message-format=json > /tmp/clippy.json
      - name: lint-gate (count ratchet)
        run: cargo run -p xtask -- lint-gate --from /tmp/clippy.json
